# As an Owner, I Have a Right to the Profits Generated by My Property

## Claim

The claim that owners have a right to the profits generated by their property seems self-evident only as long as ownership also bears the associated risks.

Under limited liability, this assumption becomes fragile. Owners can receive profits while certain losses fall on the company, employees, creditors, or the public. It must then be justified anew why profits should be private while risks are partly collective.

## Why It Matters

This note marks an institutional point at which a sustainable constitution would need to organize responsibility, ownership, power, or externalities more clearly.
